name: Databricks End-to-End
description: A full tour of Databricks Free Edition across 12 ordered stages — from Unity Catalog and Lakebase to the medallion, semantic layer, and AI/BI Genie. $0, serverless, no cloud account required.

stages.label: Connect
stages.title: Connect — point the app at your workspace

stages.label: Landing Zone
stages.title: Landing Zone — Unity Catalog, schemas, and managed volume

callout.body:
**Unity Catalog** is Databricks' governance layer — a three-level namespace (catalog → schema → table/volume) with access control, lineage, and data discovery built in. You own one catalog: `silverline`, with three schemas that mirror the medallion architecture (`bronze` / `silver` / `gold`) and a **managed volume** for files.

**Managed** means Databricks owns the storage lifecycle — drop the volume and the files are deleted. **External** means your own cloud bucket — drop the volume registration and the files are kept. For Free Edition we use managed volumes (no cloud account needed).

sections.heading: What to do in stage 02 — create the Unity Catalog landing zone
sections.body:
1. In the workspace, open the **SQL editor** (left sidebar → SQL Editor).

2. Run this block to create the catalog and medallion schemas (idempotent — safe to re-run):

   ```sql
   CREATE CATALOG IF NOT EXISTS silverline
     COMMENT 'Shared landing zone for all tutorial phases.';
   CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS silverline.bronze COMMENT 'Raw / ingested';
   CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS silverline.silver COMMENT 'Cleaned / current-state';
   CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS silverline.gold   COMMENT 'Business / serving';
   ```

3. Create the managed volume for seed files and contract PDFs:

   ```sql
   CREATE VOLUME IF NOT EXISTS silverline.bronze.files
     COMMENT 'Managed volume — seed files + contract PDFs for the RAG track.';
   ```

4. Verify your work:

   ```sql
   SHOW SCHEMAS IN silverline;       -- expect bronze, silver, gold
   SHOW VOLUMES IN silverline.bronze; -- expect files
   ```

5. Browse to **Catalog Explorer** in the UI (left sidebar → Catalog) to see `silverline` and its schemas — this is what Unity Catalog looks like.

stages.label: Project · dbt
stages.title: Project · dbt — local tooling (mise, uv, dbt via OAuth)

callout.body:
**Local tooling** is the "project" layer — `mise` (task runner), `uv` (Python package manager), and `dbt` (SQL transformations). Together they give you a reproducible, one-command dev environment for the whole tutorial.

dbt uses **OAuth** to talk to the Starter Warehouse — no PAT or password stored in any config file. The `free` profile you authenticated in stage 01 is the only credential dbt needs.

sections.heading: What to do in stage 03 — set up local tooling
sections.body:
1. In the repo at `tutorials/databricks/end-to-end/`, copy `.env.sample` to `.env` and fill in your workspace URL and Starter Warehouse ID from stage 01.

2. Run `mise run setup` — installs `dbt-databricks`, `databricks-sdk`, and `databricks-sql-connector` via uv into a local virtual environment.

3. Run `mise run dbt:debug` — proves dbt can reach the warehouse and `silverline` catalog via OAuth.
   Expect: **All checks passed!**

4. Smoke test:

   ```bash
   mise run sql 'SELECT current_catalog(), current_user()'
   ```

   Expect: `silverline | <your email>`

5. If `dbt debug` fails on auth, re-run `databricks auth login --profile free` — the cached OAuth token may have expired (they last ~50 minutes).

stages.label: Provision
stages.title: Provision — create the Lakebase PG17 autoscaling project

callout.body:
**Lakebase** is Databricks' serverless Postgres 17. An **Autoscaling project** auto-scales and idles to ~0 quota when unused — you pay (in quota) only for active connections. Auth uses **short-lived OAuth tokens** minted on demand as the Postgres password — nothing static is stored or committed.

**PG17 matters** because Lakebase CDF (native CDC) requires it. Use `postgres create-project`, not `database create-database-instance` — the latter only gives PG16.

sections.heading: What to do in stage 04 — provision the Lakebase project
sections.body:
1. Create the PG17 Autoscaling project via the Databricks CLI:

   ```bash
   databricks --profile free postgres create-project silverline-oltp \
     --json '{"spec":{"pg_version":17}}' --timeout 15m -o json
   ```

   Expect `pg_version: 17` in the output. This takes 1–2 minutes.

2. Capture the endpoint host:

   ```bash
   EP=projects/silverline-oltp/branches/production/endpoints/primary
   databricks --profile free postgres get-endpoint "$EP" -o json
   ```

   Copy the `status.hosts.host` value into your `.env` as `LAKEBASE_HOST`.

3. Mint a credential and verify connectivity:

   ```bash
   TOKEN=$(databricks --profile free postgres generate-database-credential "$EP" \
     -o json | jq -r '.token')
   # then connect with psql and run:
   SELECT version();
   # expect: PostgreSQL 17.x over SSL
   ```

4. Add to `.env`:

   ```
   LAKEBASE_DB=databricks_postgres
   LAKEBASE_USER=<your-databricks-email>
   ```

checks.errorHint: Run: databricks --profile free postgres create-project silverline-oltp --json '{"spec":{"pg_version":17}}'

callout.body:
The seed stage loads **Silverline Capital's full 9-table operational model** into Lakebase. It uses a deterministic script (`MOCK_SEED=42`) so results are identical every run — safe to re-run if anything goes wrong.

The data represents a fictional equipment lease & loan finance company's full lifecycle: customers → applications → contracts → equipment → billing → payments.

sections.heading: What to do in stage 05 — seed Lakebase
sections.body:
1. In your workspace, open **`SilverAIWolf/05-seed/05.1_seed_oltp`** (serverless) and click **Run All**. It mints a Lakebase credential via the SDK and seeds all 9 tables.

   Expected counts: `customers=60 vendors=15 equipment=220 applications=140 contracts=85 contract_assets=180 payment_schedule=2904 invoices=1452 payments=1291`

2. Run **`SilverAIWolf/05-seed/05.2_data_model`** (serverless, Run All) — shows the ERD, counts, and a segment analysis using psycopg.

3. Run **`SilverAIWolf/05-seed/05.3_documents`** (serverless, Run All) — generates contract PDFs and credit memos and writes them to `/Volumes/silverline/bronze/files/`. Verify in Catalog Explorer.

4. Once seeded, click any table tile below to query live rows from Lakebase.

**Entity-relationship overview:**

```
customers ── applications ──▶ contracts ──◀ contract_assets ▶── equipment ──▶ vendors
                                    │
                                    ├──◀ payment_schedule
                                    └──◀ invoices ──◀ payments
```

| Table | Role |
|---|---|
| `customers` | Businesses Silverline finances — segment, region, credit rating |
| `vendors` | Equipment suppliers |
| `equipment` | Individual financed assets (make, model, serial, cost) |
| `applications` | Credit pipeline — submitted → approved → booked |
| `contracts` | Booked lease/loan deals — type, status, APR, term |
| `contract_assets` | M:N bridge — which equipment backs which contract |
| `payment_schedule` | Amortization plan per period |
| `invoices` | Bills issued — open / paid / overdue |
| `payments` | Cash received against invoices |

stages.label: Data API
stages.title: Data API — expose Lakebase as a REST endpoint

callout.body:
The **Lakebase Data API** exposes your Postgres tables as a REST endpoint (PostgREST-compatible) with zero backend code. The business — or an agent — can read customers, contracts, and overdue invoices over plain HTTPS.

Auth uses **M2M OAuth** (service principal), not your user identity. The SP mints a short-lived token against your workspace and passes it as the Postgres password — same ephemeral-credential pattern as stage 04, but for non-human callers.

sections.heading: What to do in stage 06 — enable the Data API
sections.body:
1. **Enable the Data API (UI-only — no CLI toggle exists for this):** In your workspace, open **Database** (Lakebase) → click the `silverline-oltp` project → **Data API** page (under App Backend) → click **Enable Data API**.

2. **Create a Service Principal** via the CLI:

   ```bash
   databricks --profile free service-principals create \
     --display-name "silverline-data-api" -o json
   # note the applicationId

   databricks --profile free service-principal-secrets-proxy create <sp-id> -o json
   # note the .secret (shown once)
   ```

3. **Store the SP credentials** in a Databricks secret scope:

   ```bash
   databricks --profile free secrets create-scope silverline
   databricks --profile free secrets put-secret silverline data_api_sp_client_id \
     --string-value "<APP_ID>"
   databricks --profile free secrets put-secret silverline data_api_sp_secret \
     --string-value "<SECRET>"
   ```

4. **Grant the SP a Postgres role** (run as the database owner in psql or psycopg):

   ```sql
   CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS databricks_auth;
   SELECT databricks_create_role('<APP_ID>', 'SERVICE_PRINCIPAL');
   GRANT "<APP_ID>" TO authenticator;
   GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO "<APP_ID>";
   GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO "<APP_ID>";
   ```

5. **Test a REST query:** Run notebook `SilverAIWolf/06-data-api/06.1_data_api_demo` — it reads SP creds from the secret scope, mints an M2M token, and queries customers, overdue invoices, and active contracts via HTTPS. You should see JSON rows.

stages.label: Ingest
stages.title: Ingest — land Lakebase data into bronze Delta

callout.body:
**Ingest** is how OLTP data enters the Lakehouse. Lakebase is native to Databricks, so the first move is **zero-ETL**: register the project as a read-only Unity Catalog catalog and query live Postgres tables directly — no copy, no pipeline, no lag.

When you want a governed Delta copy (with history and the medallion pipeline), you land into `silverline.bronze`. This stage shows four different patterns — from the simplest (zero-ETL) to the most complete (managed CDC).

sections.heading: What to do in stage 07 — ingest Lakebase into the Lakehouse
sections.body:
1. **Register as a native UC catalog** (Claude runs this CLI step via the connect stage):

   ```bash
   databricks --profile free api post \
     "/api/2.0/postgres/catalogs?catalog_id=lakebase_silverline_oltp" \
     --json '{"spec":{"postgres_database":"databricks_postgres","branch":"projects/silverline-oltp/branches/production"}}'
   ```

   Then verify:

   ```bash
   mise run sql 'SELECT count(*) FROM lakebase_silverline_oltp.public.customers'
   ```

   Expect **60**. This is zero-ETL: live Postgres rows, no copy.

2. Run `07.1_native_catalog` — explores the live OLTP via SQL (counts, a segment join) with zero data movement.

3. Run `07.2_ctas_snapshot`:

   ```sql
   CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silverline.bronze.customers
     AS SELECT * FROM lakebase_silverline_oltp.public.customers;
   -- … repeated for all 9 tables
   ```

   This is the bronze snapshot the medallion builds on.

4. *Optional:* `07.3_watermark_cdc` (watermark-based incremental), `07.4_wal_cdc` (WAL logical decoding — delete-aware), `07.5_lakebase_cdf` (native managed CDC, requires external S3 — opt-in).

| Pattern | Notebook | Handles Deletes? | Needs Cloud? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native query (zero-ETL) | 07.1 | n/a | No |
| Full CTAS snapshot | 07.2 | Yes (rewrite) | No |
| Watermark CDC | 07.3 | No | No |
| WAL logical-decoding CDC | 07.4 | Yes | No |
| Lakebase CDF (native managed) | 07.5 | Yes | Yes (S3 for CDF destination) |

callout.body:
The **medallion architecture** is the standard Lakehouse data quality pattern. Raw data from Lakebase lands in **Bronze** as-is — append-only, no transforms. A dbt pipeline then cleans, de-dupes, and joins it into **Silver** (conformed types, nulls handled). Another pass aggregates it into **Gold**: business-level tables like `gold_segment_portfolio` that BI tools and ML models query directly.

**`bronze`** (raw / ingested) → **`silver`** (cleaned / conformed) → **`gold`** (business / serving)

Each layer is a **Delta Lake** table in the Databricks SQL warehouse — a different store from Lakebase Postgres. Delta gives you ACID transactions, time travel, and incremental processing on top of cloud object storage.

sections.heading: What to do in stage 08 — three ways to build silver + gold
sections.body:
1. Run **`08.1_build_ddl`** — defines empty `silver_*` and `gold_*_nb` tables (structure only, no data yet).

2. Run **`08.2_build_dbt`** — creates and runs a Databricks Job with a native `dbt task`. dbt reads `dbt_project/` and outputs canonical `gold_segment_portfolio` and `gold_contract_aging`.

3. Run **`08.3_build_sdp`** — creates and runs a Lakeflow/SDP declarative pipeline from `sdp_project/`. Uses `@dlt.table` + `@dlt.expect_or_drop` quality checks → `*_sdp` tables.

4. Run **`08.4_build_notebook`** — runs a Workflow Job that `INSERT OVERWRITE`s the `_nb` tables defined in step 1 — the notebook/ELT approach.

5. Run **`08.5_parity`** — compares all three gold outputs side-by-side with symmetric `EXCEPT` diffs. All diffs = 0 → identical results.

| Approach | Tool | Key trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| Notebook (_nb) | Workflows | Most control, schedule it yourself |
| dbt (canonical) | dbt + Job | Best portability + docs/tests |
| SDP/Lakeflow (_sdp) | Declarative | Managed quality, least code to operate |

Each layer is a **Delta Lake** table — ACID transactions, time travel (`VERSION AS OF N`), and lineage tracked automatically in Unity Catalog.

stages.label: Refresh · Live
stages.title: Refresh · Live — change the source, watch it stream

callout.body:
**Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY** is a built-in pub-sub channel. Three database triggers on `customers`, `contracts`, and `invoices` call `pg_notify('silverline_changes', …)` on every INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE. The server holds a dedicated connection that called `LISTEN silverline_changes` at startup — so changes arrive in microseconds with no polling.

Those events are forwarded to the browser as a **GraphQL subscription over WebSocket**, which is why they appear instantly. Hit **⚡ Simulate a change** in the live feed below to watch an INSERT → UPDATE → DELETE sequence land in real time.

sections.heading: What to do in stage 09 — refresh the pipeline after a source change
sections.body:
1. Run **`09.1_add_triggers`** — installs `pg_notify` triggers on `customers`, `contracts`, and `invoices`. After this, the live feed below will show changes in real time.

2. Apply the deterministic change-set (modifies 3 customers, updates 2 contracts, adds 5 invoices):

   ```bash
   mise run apply-changeset
   ```

   Watch the live feed light up with the events.

3. Re-ingest the changed tables into bronze:

   ```bash
   mise run ingest:refresh
   # or run 09.2_refresh_ingest in the workspace
   ```

4. Re-run the dbt medallion to rebuild silver + gold:

   ```bash
   mise run dbt:run
   ```

5. Verify lineage end-to-end:

   ```sql
   SELECT count(*) FROM silverline.silver.silver_invoices;   -- should be > before
   SELECT count(*) FROM silverline.gold.gold_contract_aging;  -- should include new invoices
   ```

stages.label: Business Layer
stages.title: Business Layer — document gold tables for Genie

callout.body:
The gold tables exist but aren't documented. **COMMENTs on tables and columns** are what Genie and AI assistants read to understand the schema — "billed" maps to `total_billed`, "overdue" maps to `overdue_amount`. An undocumented gold layer means worse Genie answers.

A `customer_360` view rolls contract aging up to the customer grain — one row per customer with their overdue balance and total billed. This is what a collections team or a Genie query would naturally ask for.

sections.heading: What to do in stage 10 — document the business layer
sections.body:
1. Add table and column COMMENTs to the gold tables (paste into SQL editor → Run):

   ```sql
   COMMENT ON TABLE silverline.gold.gold_segment_portfolio IS
     'Portfolio by customer segment — contract counts, principal, APR, residual.';
   ALTER TABLE silverline.gold.gold_segment_portfolio ALTER COLUMN segment
     COMMENT 'Customer business segment.';
   ALTER TABLE silverline.gold.gold_segment_portfolio ALTER COLUMN total_principal
     COMMENT 'Sum of contract principal financed for the segment.';
   -- (same pattern for each column on both tables)
   ```

2. Add COMMENTs to `gold_contract_aging` columns: `contract_id`, `overdue_amount`, `open_amount`, `paid_amount`, `total_billed`.

3. Create the `customer_360` view (customer profile + contract aging, rolled to customer grain):

   ```sql
   CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW silverline.gold.customer_360
   COMMENT 'Per-customer collections view: profile + contract aging.'
   AS
   SELECT c.customer_id, c.legal_name, c.segment, c.region, c.credit_rating,
          sum(a.overdue_amount) AS overdue_amount,
          sum(a.total_billed)   AS total_billed
   FROM silverline.gold.gold_contract_aging a
   JOIN silverline.silver.silver_contracts ct ON ct.contract_id = a.contract_id
   JOIN silverline.silver.silver_customers c  ON c.customer_id  = ct.customer_id
   GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.legal_name, c.segment, c.region, c.credit_rating;
   ```

4. Verify: run `DESCRIBE TABLE EXTENDED silverline.gold.gold_segment_portfolio` and check that comments appear. Browse the table in **Catalog Explorer** to see them in the UI.

stages.label: Semantic · Metrics
stages.title: Semantic · Metrics — governed MEASURE() Metric View

callout.body:
`gold_segment_portfolio` answers one question (portfolio by segment). A **Metric View** answers *every* slice of the same governed billing measures — by region, credit rating, contract type, month — from one definition.

`MEASURE()` functions define KPIs *once* so they can't drift between dashboards, notebooks, and Genie. When Genie answers "total billed by region" it uses the same `MEASURE(total_billed)` as the chart tile — they can never disagree.

sections.heading: What to do in stage 11 — create the Metric View
sections.body:
1. Open `sql/portfolio_metrics.sql` in the repo — review the measures (`total_billed`, `invoice_count`, `overdue_amount`, `overdue_ratio`) and dimensions (`segment`, `region`, `credit_rating`, `contract_type`, `status`, `invoice_date`).

2. Paste the full SQL into the **Databricks SQL editor** and run. The `WITH METRICS` YAML block is finicky over the CLI — use the editor.

3. Query the metric view — one definition, any slice:

   ```sql
   -- By segment:
   SELECT segment, MEASURE(total_billed) AS total_billed
   FROM silverline.gold.portfolio_metrics GROUP BY segment;

   -- By region and contract type (no new SQL logic, just a different GROUP BY):
   SELECT region, contract_type, MEASURE(overdue_ratio) AS overdue_ratio
   FROM silverline.gold.portfolio_metrics GROUP BY region, contract_type;
   ```

4. Verify the metric view matches the physical gold total:

   ```sql
   WITH m AS (SELECT MEASURE(total_billed) tb FROM silverline.gold.portfolio_metrics),
        g AS (SELECT sum(total_billed)     tb FROM silverline.gold.gold_contract_aging)
   SELECT (SELECT tb FROM m) AS metric_view_billed,
          (SELECT tb FROM g) AS gold_billed,
          CASE WHEN (SELECT tb FROM m) <=> (SELECT tb FROM g)
               THEN 'MATCH' ELSE 'DRIFT' END
   ```

   Expect: **MATCH**

5. *Optional:* run `11.2_why_metrics` notebook to see the "average of averages" trap — a hand-rolled overdue ratio can be 7.5× wrong vs the governed `MEASURE()`.

callout.body:
**AI/BI dashboards and Genie** both read the same `portfolio_metrics` Metric View — so a chart tile and a Genie answer for "total billed" can never disagree. Genie translates plain English into SQL using the governed `MEASURE()` definitions, not guessed `SUM()` joins.

This is the payoff of the whole pipeline: a non-technical user asks a question in plain English and gets back an exact, governed answer that matches the dashboard — because both are powered by the same semantic layer you built in stage 11.

sections.heading: What to do in stage 12 — AI/BI dashboard + Genie
sections.body:
1. Create the **AI/BI dashboard** from `dashboards/portfolio_dashboard.lvdash.json`:

   ```bash
   databricks lakeview create \
     --display-name "Silverline Capital — Portfolio (governed metrics)" \
     --warehouse-id "$DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID" \
     --serialized-dashboard "$(cat dashboards/portfolio_dashboard.lvdash.json)"

   databricks lakeview publish <dashboard_id> \
     --warehouse-id "$DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID" --embed-credentials
   ```

   Open it in the UI and confirm three tiles: billed by segment, billed by contract type, overdue ratio by region — all using `MEASURE(...)`.

2. Create the **Genie space** from `dashboards/genie_space.json`:

   ```bash
   databricks genie create-space "$DATABRICKS_WAREHOUSE_ID" \
     "$(cat dashboards/genie_space.json)" \
     --title "Silverline Capital — Portfolio Genie"
   ```

3. Open the Genie space and ask in natural language:
   - *"What is the total billed by segment?"* → expect `MEASURE(total_billed) GROUP BY segment`
   - *"Which region has the highest overdue ratio?"* → expect `MEASURE(overdue_ratio) GROUP BY region`

4. Run `12.2_genie_programmatic` notebook — Genie as a programmatic service: SDK (`w.genie.start_conversation_and_wait`), multi-turn, CLI (`databricks genie start-conversation`), and an `ai_query()` call against a credit memo.

| Without semantic layer | With Metric View + Genie |
|---|---|
| Genie guesses `SUM()` / joins → can be wrong | Uses `MEASURE(total_billed)` → exact, governed |
| Dashboard SQL + Genie SQL can drift | Both reference the same measure definition |
| "Overdue ratio" reimplemented per consumer | One definition → dashboard == Genie == gold |
